extracted.intended_audience: CIHR Project Grant peer reviewers, peer review committee members, and applicants to the CIHR Project Grant program (health researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation standards for committee-based peer review of CIHR Project Grant applications, describing reviewer responsibilities, evaluation criteria, rating scales, conflict-of-interest and confidentiality rules, committee procedures, and applicant submission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary evaluation goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assess the quality, the potential impact of the proposed research, and the research-related activities in accordance with the evaluation criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are selected to have the required experience and expertise (individually and collectively). Reviewers evaluate applications within the context of the program's objectives and are grouped into Peer Review Committees based on expertise and topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex- and Gender-Based Analysis (SGBA) assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are asked to explicitly assess whether the integration of sex (as a biological variable) and/or gender (as a socio-cultural factor) is a strength, a weakness or not applicable to the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide comments justifying the assessment and recommendations to improve integration of sex/gender where appropriate; consult CIHR SGBA resources and complete SGBA training modules; include SGBA certificate as mandatory appendix where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge Translation (KT) expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: CIHR expects researchers to disseminate findings and facilitate their translation into improved health, products/services, and/or strengthened health systems; integrated KT requires stakeholder engagement throughout the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For end-of-grant KT select appropriate dissemination vehicles for the intended knowledge-user audience; for non-research knowledge users, comprehensive dissemination strategies are expected; costs of dissemination are eligible expenditures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Access policy compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant recipients must adhere to the Tri-Agency Open Access Policy on Publications ensuring research papers and bio-molecular data generated from CIHR funding are freely accessible online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should be aware of open access responsibilities when assessing dissemination plans and outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of productivity and progress (DORA-aligned)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are to assess productivity and progress broadly by taking into consideration a range of contributions and impacts and the context of the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider publications, reports, books, guidelines, datasets, code, tools, training and mentorship, volunteerism, community engagement, standards, software and commercialized products, policy/practice influence, health and societal outcomes, and culturally safe research; consider context (leave history, career stage, area of research, experiential knowledge, diverse career paths, family responsibilities, pandemic impact). Do not use metrics (publications/citations, journal impact factors) in isolation as surrogate measures of quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Information provided by applicants is protected and must not be disclosed or used for other purposes; committee members must not communicate with applicants about reviews or application status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breaches may result in CIHR investigation and reporting to the federal Privacy Commissioner's Office; identity of reviewers is not revealed to applicants; committee membership lists are published after funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members must identify and address conflicts between review duties and private/professional interests according to the Conflict of Interest and Confidentiality Policy (COIC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicts include: relatives/close friends; potential financial gain/loss; long-standing scientific or personal differences; current affiliation with applicant's institution; close professional affiliation in last six years (frequent interactions, supervisor/trainee relationship, collaborations, shared funding, employment by applicant's institution); any reason a member feels unable to provide impartial review. Members in conflict must leave the meeting when the application is discussed. CIHR staff resolve uncertainties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness requirements for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must exercise rigorous judgment, be impartial and reasonable, take into account the context of each application, and provide constructive, quality reviews that point out strengths and weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should help applicants understand factors contributing to their rating and provide balanced assessments aligned with program objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: CIHR ensures transparency by requiring reviews and Scientific Officer notes to be shared with applicants and publishing committee membership lists and funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All applications are evaluated using application requirements and review criteria established for the competition; SO notes capture committee deliberations and are shared with applicants where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application assignment to peer review committees
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are initially assigned to the applicant's first-choice committee; CIHR staff, Chairs and Scientific Officers review and may reassign applications based on committee mandates; final assignment authority rests with CIHR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should review committee mandates before registering; assigned committee may not be the 1st or 2nd choice. Registrations include justification for chosen committees; committee Chairs/SOs review alignment and can split committees if application pressure is high.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment to reviewers and reviewer workload
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application is assigned to three reviewers based on declared expertise; each reviewer receives a maximum of 8 to 10 applications (reduced for ECR reviewers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers declare expertise levels (High/Medium/Low/Not enough) and conflicts in advance. External referees may be solicited when specific expertise is required; external referees see only assigned applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer and committee member selection criteria (diversity)
rubrics_metrics.description: CIHR strives for panel diversity by recruiting members representing institutions of varying sizes/regions, official languages capability, balanced membership by sex where possible, and members at different career stages (including early career researchers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection considers national representation and proportionate gender representation; language capabilities ensure applications in either official language can be evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications for Chairs and Scientific Officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Chairs and Scientific Officers should have significant peer review experience, Independent Investigator status, and recent tri-council (or equivalent) funding within last 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant experience is defined as previous Committee Chair/SO roles or multiple review activities; past peer review performance must have met high standards. Recruitment may use combination of criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers should have Independent Investigator status, at least one recent federally funded (or equivalent) peer-reviewed grant as PI, at least two peer review roles at CIHR or other recognized organizations, and expertise within CIHR's mandate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruitment may include Knowledge Users and those with lived experience; criteria may be combined as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory reviewer training and learning modules
rubrics_metrics.description: All committee members are expected to complete training modules such as Conducting Quality Reviews, Bias in Peer Review, and SGBA learning modules; methodological modules are expected where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module durations and specific choices depend on role; Knowledge Users are recommended to complete Assessing Sex and Gender Integration in Peer Review. Training supports consistency and bias mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and self-contained application requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Research proposals must be self-contained, adhere to formatting requirements, and not rely on hyperlinks or external drives; English proposals up to 10 pages, French up to 12 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures, tables, charts and photographs may be within page limits; failure to comply with formatting can negatively impact evaluation and may lead to withdrawal. Hyperlinks and Google Drive links should not be accessed during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of Progress expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: A two-page narrative that outlines activities, contributions, impacts supporting the current application; explains how the application fits the overarching research program and why requested funds are needed; and clarifies overlap/distinction from funds already held or pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May describe impact of leaves, career stage, pandemic, family responsibilities; reviewers assess productivity broadly and consider context. The Summary is narrative, not a detailed funding accounting (funding details are in the CV).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of resubmissions and responses to previous reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmissions are to be treated as new applications; applicants may provide an optional response (up to 2 pages) to previous reviewers' comments but must include all previous reviews and SO notes in the response package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must not consider previous ratings when evaluating the current application. If previous reviews are not included when a response is provided, attachments will be removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: CV evaluation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assess CV(s) together with Most Significant Contributions to judge the team's ability to deliver project objectives and assess productivity broadly in context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Academic applicants must use CIHR Biosketch CV; non-academics, Indigenous organizations, knowledge users and international applicants may use Applicant Profile CV (max 3 pages). Failure to provide correct CV format may negatively impact evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory and optional appendices policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must read all Other Application Materials provided. Mandatory appendices include SGBA certificate, dean's letter for pending appointment, employer letter for international researchers paid from the grant, and letters of community support for Indigenous health research; optional appendices include letters of collaboration. Certain appendices are no longer accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendices no longer accepted include patient information sheets (for RCTs), publications, questionnaires/surveys/consent forms, supplementary tables/charts/figures/photos, and any other documents. Non-eligible appendices should be flagged to CIHR staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completing the review in ResearchNet (required review components)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must submit: a global rating using the rating scale; top (competitive) or bottom (non-competitive) group selection; a summary of the research proposal; justification of the rating with strengths/weaknesses including sex/gender integration assessment; an assessment of SGBA strength/weakness/not applicable; and a budget recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews must be written in reviewers' own words, be original, and use gender-neutral/inclusive language. Inappropriate reviews (sarcastic, flippant, arrogant, or factually incorrect regarding CIHR policies) may be removed by CIHR. Save work often due to ResearchNet time-outs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rating scale and descriptors
rubrics_metrics.description: A numeric rating scale with descriptors: Outstanding (4.5–4.9), Excellent (4.0–4.4), Good (3.5–3.9), Fair (3.0–3.4), Poor (0.0–2.9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each descriptor includes definition/examples: 'Outstanding' excels in most/all aspects with minimal shortcomings; 'Excellent' excels in many aspects with minor limitations; 'Good' excels in some aspects but needs work; 'Fair' broadly addresses aspects but requires major revisions (will not be funded); 'Poor' has significant flaws (will not be funded). Ratings are provided to one decimal place. Initial ratings are submitted in advance and can be revised during meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlining criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be streamlined (removed from discussion) if: (1) average reviewers' scores place the application in the bottom 60% of all applications in the committee; (2) at least one reviewer identified the application as non-competitive (bottom); and (3) there is no objection from any committee member to streamline the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Streamlined applications still receive written reviewer reports but no detailed SO notes. Streamlining decisions are informed by pre-meeting averages and top/bottom selections; additional applications may be identified for streamlining during the meeting. Committee objections will trigger discussion. Streamlined applications may have an initial average above 3.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee meeting assessment procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-streamlined applications: the primary reviewer presents their assessment (strengths/weaknesses including SGBA), two secondary reviewers follow, external reviews are read if provided, Chair opens discussion, SO reads back SO notes, and the Chair seeks a consensus rating from the three reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If consensus cannot be reached, Chair usually uses the mean of the reviewers' ratings (rounded to one decimal). The Chair does not rate or vote. Committee members not in conflict vote (+/- 0.5 of consensus rating). Scientific Officers capture discussion in SO notes and do not vote or rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget recommendation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The budget requested will not be factored into the scientific assessment and rating. However, reviewers must provide a specific budget recommendation detailing whether requested resources are appropriate, taking into account funds already held or pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should provide clear and detailed reasons for any recommended budget or term cuts. CIHR reserves the right to determine the final amount awarded. Budget concerns that bear on scientific merit may be flagged but should not bias the rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagging and handling special issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues related to ethics, eligibility, human pluripotent stem cell research and other concerns must be flagged for CIHR attention and should not unduly influence the scientific rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flagged applications are marked pending until applicants provide required information. Flagged issues should be recorded in SO notes; discussions around flagged issues should be captured objectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Officer (SO) notes standards
rubrics_metrics.description: SO Notes should provide insight into committee discussions, be clear and concise, give objective and constructive feedback, include strengths and weaknesses, align with DORA, address issues that had greatest impact on evaluation, and reconcile reviewer disagreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SO reads back notes for validation before consensus rating; SOs finalize and post notes within 5 business days after the committee meeting. SOs do not vote or rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conduct and language expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews must be constructive, original, written in the reviewer's own words, and use gender-neutral and gender-inclusive language when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid copying text from the application or previous reviews; avoid sarcastic, flippant, arrogant or inappropriate comments; reviewers may be asked to revise reviews within 5 business days after the meeting. Use inclusive terminology (e.g., 'people of all genders' rather than binary terms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indigenous Health Research and Iterative Peer Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications focusing on ethical and culturally competent research involving Indigenous Peoples may be reviewed by the Indigenous Health Research (IHR) Committee and may be eligible for the Iterative Peer Review Process, which allows applicants to provide minor clarifications to become fundable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific eligibility requirements apply and are described in the funding opportunity; letters of community support from Indigenous partners are mandatory appendices when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer in Training (RiT) program participation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The RiT program allows Early Career Researchers to participate as Mentees or ECR reviewers: Mentees conduct practice reviews, attend the meeting, present one review; ECR reviewers (with at least one recent PI-funded grant) participate as full reviewers but with reduced application loads (up to five) and may present later in the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RiT participants receive supportive resources; specific roles/responsibilities for Mentor/Mentee/ECR reviewer are detailed on the RiT webpage. RiT reviewers may revise reviews within 5 business days after the meeting.
